name: adapt
description: The suite's adaptation loop — turn observed failures and repeated friction from real runs into permanent, evidence-backed changes to the suite itself. Use after retros, when review findings escape a gate, when the finder misses, or when absorbed skills need promotion.

name: brief
description: Turn a raw request into an approved problem brief. Use when a request is bigger than a one-line fix or its real problem is unstated — before research, PRD, or any design work.

name: data-viz
description: Design and build data visualizations that tell the truth — chart selection by question and perceptual accuracy, rendering technology by scale, established layout algorithms, and chart accessibility. Use for charts, graphs, dashboards, plots, and any data presentation surface.

name: debug
description: Diagnose bugs and performance regressions with a red-capable feedback loop before any theory. Use when something fails, breaks, or regresses — and when fixes have already failed once.

name: define-product
description: Define the product layer — PRD, personas, and user stories with checkable acceptance criteria. Use when a brief is approved and a new product or user-facing feature needs its requirements fixed before design and engineering begin.

name: design
description: The design phase — DESIGN.md constitution, user flows, keyframe approval, component discovery, and bounded council review. Use for any user-facing surface being built, redesigned, or given a new visual direction.

name: gluttony
description: Absorb an external skill repository into this suite — audit every skill in it, verdict each one, and adapt what survives into suite conventions. Slash-command only; the argument is the repository URL.

name: grill
description: Stress-test a plan, design, or decision tree one question at a time until every branch resolves. Use when a plan has unexplored decisions, hidden assumptions, or trade-offs nobody has named — before spec or PRD work hardens it.

name: implement
description: Execute tickets as bounded, test-first, verifiable slices. Use when implementing from a spec and ticket graph, whether as the orchestrator's worker or directly — including prototype work and receiving-review fixes.

name: mcp-builder
description: Design, implement, and evaluate Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers in TypeScript or Python with strict tool naming, schemas, and test harnesses. Use when building or testing MCP integrations.

name: model
description: Model the domain, data, and interfaces — DOMAIN.md, ERD.md, and API.md as first-class artifacts. Use when a project has entities with lifecycles, persisted data, schema changes, or a boundary other systems consume.

name: orchestrate
description: The orchestrator protocol for the main agent. Use whenever work is delegated to subagents or external worker agents, run in parallel, or accepted from a worker — packets, report schema, dual review, rework loop, escalation.

name: recon
description: Reverse-engineer an existing product into a buildable map — screen and flow inventory, inferred data model with evidence, and a weighted feature matrix. Use when the work starts from a product that already exists: a competitor to rebuild, a reference app to match, or a legacy system nobody documented.

name: research
description: Investigate a question against primary sources and capture the findings as a durable file. Use when a decision depends on facts the team does not hold — library capabilities, API behaviour, standards, prior art.

name: retro
description: Close the loop after a ship, a failure, or a capped loop — record what the artifacts say happened and file each lesson where the next run will read it. Use at the end of every significant run.

name: review
description: Review work against its contract — two-axis review for code and artifacts, blind doubt review for risky decisions, verdicts recorded per acceptance criterion. Use before accepting delegated work, merging, or standing behind a non-trivial decision.

name: setup-workspace
description: One-time setup of a repository for the rnov24 workflow. Use when a repo will be worked on with this suite for the first time — artifact layout, tracker conventions, glossary, and the CONSTRAINTS.md quality floor.

name: ship
description: Ship finished work — launch readiness, git discipline, pull requests, and the human grant for irreversible actions. Use when verified work is ready to merge, release, or deploy.

name: spec
description: Synthesise the conversation and the upstream artifacts into one executable spec. Use when a feature or change is understood well enough to hand to implementers and needs a single document that settles what will be built.

name: study
description: Extract a design's DNA — palette, type roles, structure, motion, rhythm — from a screenshot or a public URL into a design-study artifact the design skill can build from.

name: tickets
description: Break a spec into tracer-bullet tickets with blocking edges. Use when a spec is approved and work must be scheduled across sessions or workers — each ticket independently verifiable, the graph computable into a parallel frontier.

name: using-rnov-skills
description: The router for the rnov24 suite. Use at the start of any product, design, or engineering task to decide which flow applies, which artifacts the task needs, and which skill runs next.

name: verify
description: Evidence before claims — run the checks fresh and read the output before anything is called done, fixed, or passing. Use at the end of every implement phase and before any completion claim to the human.
